newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress party re-elects chief.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress party re-elects chief.

text.p: India's Congress party on Thursday re-elected veteran politician Sitaram Kesri as its president, party officials said.

The voting for the politically influential post was held on Monday. It was only the third election in the 112-year history of India's oldest political party, traditionally dominated by charismatic leaders.

Once the driving force behind the movement against colonial rule, Congress has ruled India for all but five years since independence in 1947, with former prime ministers Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi in power for 37 years.
Kesri, 76, swept aside challenges from two younger party leaders who ran on a platform of rejuvenating the ailing party that was ejected from power last year.
